Project Overview & Business Case

The COVID-19 pandemic showed how difficult it can be for hospitals to handle many patients at the same time. Which is why I propose an idea to bring appropriate healthcare services closer to patients, instead of requiring everyone to visit a hospital.

91.6%

Canadian acute care beds occupied before the pandemic, according to the cited National Post article [1].

560K

Fewer surgeries performed in Canada from March 2020 to June 2021 compared with pre-pandemic levels [2].

337K

Approximate Fraser Valley population in the 2021 Census, across more than 13,000 km² [3].

The pandemic affected both COVID-19 patients and people waiting for other types of care. In addition, residents of a large region like the Fraser Valley may have different levels of access to nearby healthcare services, especially in rural communities.

The proposed network would combine scheduled mobile clinics, appropriate home visits, an online appointment platform, healthcare workers and regional support facilities. It would complement existing services, including Fraser Health virtual care [4], rather than replace hospitals or emergency departments.

Project purpose: Make healthcare more accessible and help the region prepare for future public health emergencies. Proposed completion: December 31, 2029.

Project Goals & Objectives

Create a mobile and online healthcare network supporting Fraser Valley communities during normal times and future pandemics.

  1. Provide mobile healthcare services to communities across the Fraser Valley.
  2. Allow patients to request suitable home visits through an online platform.
  3. Reduce unnecessary travel.
  4. Support existing hospitals with additional non-emergency healthcare options.
  5. Improve access for elderly patients, people with disabilities, and rural residents.
  6. Build a website and app for booking, communication and service information.
  7. Train healthcare workers to provide care safely outside traditional clinics.
The target of approximately 1,000 vehicles is an initial planning assumption. Final quantities and vehicle types depend on feasibility, costs, staffing and community needs.

Project Scope

✓ Included

  • Purchasing and preparing mobile healthcare vehicles
  • Medical equipment and supplies
  • MediGo website and mobile app
  • Scheduling and team assignment system
  • Regional support facilities
  • Healthcare staff hiring and training
  • Potential healthcare partnerships
  • Service and technology testing
  • Emergency operating procedures

✕ Not included

  • Constructing a new general hospital
  • Developing or manufacturing vaccines
  • Replacing existing hospitals or emergency services
  • Operating indefinitely without future funding
  • Automatically dispatching a vehicle to every request

Main Project Components

🚐

Clinic on Wheels

Scheduled mobile clinics visit communities on a regular basis and provide approved basic health assessments, vaccinations, selected tests and follow up.

🏠

On-Demand Home Visits

Smaller healthcare teams may visit patients at home after a qualified staff reviews and approves the request.

📱

Website & Mobile App

Online booking, clinic locations, home visit requests, virtual consultations, notifications and a staff management dashboard.

🏥

Healthcare Connections

Potential collaboration with existing hospitals and laboratories for samples, referrals and advanced treatment when needed.

How a home visit could work

  1. A patient submits a home visit request on MediGo Web or by phone app.
  2. A qualified staff reviews the request and determines whether a home visit is appropriate.
  3. An available mobile medical team is assigned, if approved.
  4. The team provides services and arranges follow up or a referral if necessary.
Clinical safety: Mobile clinics are not ambulances or a replacement for emergency departments. Serious cases must be referred to appropriate emergency or specialist care. (I don't think we could replaced emergency service like 911 with UFV current scale)

Pre-Initiation Tasks

The project is still a proposal. These tasks need to be investigated before formal approval and detailed implementation planning.

  1. Identify the healthcare problem. Research COVID-19 impacts, hospital demand and care outside hospitals.
  2. Research Fraser Valley. Study population, geology, existing healthcare facilities and communities.
  3. Study existing services. Review virtual care, home healthcare, mobile services and community clinics.
  4. Develop the mobile clinic concept. Decide vehicle types, services and staffing needs.
  5. Plan the online platform. Define booking, home visits, clinic location and staff scheduling features.
  6. Identify stakeholders. Assess possible partners across healthcare, government, UFV and technology.
  7. Estimate costs. Research vehicles, equipment, facilities, staffing, software and operations.
  8. Check feasibility. Examine cost, timeframe, regulations, privacy, staffing and sustainability.
  9. Identify risks. Address maintenance, staffing, technology, operating cost and rural access.
  10. Submit for approval. Present the project concept and research to the proposed sponsor.

Project Management Considerations

Three Spheres of Systems Management

Business

$1B budget, community healthcare needs, financial feasibility and expected benefits.

Organization

Coordination among UFV, potential healthcare partners, healthcare workers, IT staff and communities.

Technology

Mobile vehicles, medical equipment, website, app, scheduling, safety and security.

All three spheres are connected: vehicles alone will not work without employees and reliable management systems.

Four Frames of Organizations

▦

Structural Frame

Reporting relationships, roles, responsibilities and the project team.

♧

Human Resource Frame

Healthcare workers, training, employee needs and motivation.

⚖

Political Frame

Stakeholder interests, funding decisions, negotiations and approvals.

✦

Symbolic Frame

Project identity, UFV community values and accessible healthcare.

Project Champion

A senior UFV leadership representative will be the Project Champion (Maybe our Chaacha?). This person would support the concept, help communicate its benefits and find collaborations from potential healthcare, government and funding partners.

The Project Manager (me) would manage the schedule, budget, employees, risks and day to day project activities.

Project Life Cycle & Process Groups

The Waterfall approach will be used for activities such as vehicle procurement, regional facility preparation, and major equipment purchases because these activities require clear requirements and approvals. An Agile approach will be used for developing the website and mobile app. For example, the project team could first develop appointment booking and clinic location features, test them with users, and then add home visit requests and other functions.

Process GroupHow it applies
InitiatingExplain concept and request approval
PlanningDefine budget, schedule, scope, risks and service requirements
ExecutingPurchase vehicles, build app, recruit staff, prepare operations
Monitoring & ControllingTrack progress, costs, quality and risks
ClosingConfirm readiness, complete testing and hand over to approved operators

Preliminary Cost Estimate

A proposed CAD $1 billion investment in vehicles, equipment, digital infrastructure, support facilities and initial operations.

$1,000,000,000 CAD

Early proposal-stage estimate, not a confirmed procurement or operating budget.

CategoryEstimateRelative scale
Mobile healthcare vehicles$280M
Regional support hubs and facilities$60M
Additional medical equipment and supplies$70M
UFV MediGo website, app and IT systems$40M
Healthcare workforce$300M
Initial service operations and vehicle maintenance$140M
Rural access and community outreach$15M
Staff training and emergency preparation$20M
Project management and administration$25M
Safety, privacy, testing and quality control$15M
Contingency reserve$35M
Total Project Budget$1,000M100% of proposed budget

Four main cost assumptions

Mobile healthcare vehicles $280M

1,000 vehicles at an estimated $260,000 each, plus $20M for accessories and related purchasing expenses. Vehicle price range from supplier reference [5]: CAD $205K–$315K.

1,000 × $260K + $20M = $280M
Regional support facilities $60M

Assume four hubs of 50,000 sq. ft. each at $175/sq. ft., with another $25M for land, preparation and facility needs. Benchmark from construction source [6].

4 × 50,000 × $175 + $25M = $60M
Medical equipment & supplies $70M

Assume $50,000 of additional equipment per vehicle plus $20M in supplies and replacement equipment. Individual equipment types are referenced against supplier [7].

1,000 × $50K + $20M = $70M
Website, app & IT $40M

Preliminary allowance for software development, scheduling, servers, security, data management, integration and technical support. No supplier quotation is confirmed.

Planning assumption: $40M
Other estimated costs: $550M. This includes healthcare workforce, initial operations, maintenance, community outreach, training, project management, safety testing and contingency. The staffing and operating model still need detailed validation.

SWOT Analysis

Strengths

  • Brings care closer to patients
  • Supports communities without a new hospital in every location
  • Connects clinics with online booking
  • Useful in normal times and emergencies
  • Could reduce some unnecessary hospital visits

Weaknesses

  • Requires many qualified healthcare workers
  • Vehicles need regular maintenance
  • Services depend on communications and scheduling
  • Long-term operating costs may be high

Opportunities

  • Improve rural healthcare access
  • Create healthcare and technology jobs
  • Potential university collaboration
  • Improve preparedness for a future pandemic

Threats

  • Healthcare professional shortages
  • Increasing costs
  • Technical or cybersecurity problems
  • Severe weather disruption
  • Low patient adoption
  • Regulatory approval challenges

Project Success Criteria

  1. The mobile healthcare network is ready for approved operations.
  2. The UFV MediGo website and app have been tested and approved.
  3. Patients can access appointments online and by phone.
  4. Teams have appropriate equipment and training.
  5. Services can operate in planned Fraser Valley coverage areas.
  6. Patient information is protected through approved procedures.
  7. The service can expand during a public-health emergency.
This site is just a proposal from me (a student). It is not an official UFV or Fraser Health project, healthcare provider, operational booking service, or promise of funding.
